title: Calculating wave speed (v = fλ)
keyIdea: Wave speed v equals frequency f times wavelength λ (v = f × λ). Rearrange to λ = v ÷ f or f = v ÷ λ. Convert to Hz and metres before calculating so the product is in m/s.
familyTip: Ask: if a wave has frequency 5 Hz and wavelength 2 m, what is its speed? Then flip it: speed 340 m/s, frequency 680 Hz — what is λ?

visual.caption: Wave-equation idea or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: reveal v = f × λ, calculate speed, rearrange for λ, convert kHz/cm, catch sum/unit mix-ups, then challenge.

kid: A wave has a speed v, a frequency f (how many waves per second) and a wavelength λ (the length of one wave). They link by v = f × λ.
If you know two of them, you can find the third. Speed is frequency times wavelength. Wavelength is speed divided by frequency. Frequency is speed divided by wavelength.
Units matter. Frequency in hertz (Hz) and wavelength in metres (m) give speed in metres per second (m/s). Change kilohertz to hertz and centimetres to metres before you multiply.
Do not add frequency and wavelength. Speed is a product, not a sum.
adult: Ages 13 to 15. KS3 waves / NGSS HS-PS4-1: calculate and rearrange v = f × λ with coherent units. This is the calculation lesson, not the rope-properties lab.
Words: wave speed, frequency, wavelength, hertz, metres per second, rearrange. Common mistakes: v = f + λ; mixing kHz with cm; using λ = v × f; thinking Hz × m is not m/s.
In the lab the learner reveals the equation, multiplies for v, divides for λ, converts units, spots the sum myth, and orders the method.

practice.hint: Speed is a product of frequency and wavelength.
practice.explain: The wave equation is v = f × λ. Adding or subtracting mixes the quantities wrongly.

practice.prompt: f = {a} Hz and λ = {b} m. Speed v in m/s?
practice.hint: Multiply the frequency in hertz by the wavelength in metres.
Spot the false link between v, f and λ.
practice.explain: Speed is not the sum of frequency and wavelength. The true links are v = f × λ and λ = v ÷ f.

practice.prompt: v = {a} m/s and f = {b} Hz. Wavelength λ in m?
practice.hint: Rearrange: wavelength equals speed divided by frequency (λ = v ÷ f).

practice.prompt: Before calculating with 2 kHz and 15 cm you should…
practice.hint: Put frequency in Hz and wavelength in metres.

pool.hint: What unit does the product of frequency and wavelength carry?
pool.explain: Frequency in Hz (1/s) times length in m gives speed in m/s.

pool.prompt: To find frequency from v and λ use…
pool.hint: Rearrange v = f × λ for f.
pool.explain: Divide both sides by λ: f = v ÷ λ.

pool.hint: Multiply frequency by wavelength to get speed in metres per second.
Remember kilo means one thousand when converting kilohertz to hertz.

pool.prompt: Correct first step on mixed units is…
pool.explain: Convert first so v = f × λ uses Hz and metres.

pool.prompt: v = {a} m/s and f = {a} Hz. Wavelength λ in m?
pool.hint: Divide speed by frequency when both values match; λ becomes 1 m.
pool.explain: When v and f are the same number, λ = v ÷ f = {a} ÷ {a} = 1 m.

pool.prompt: This lesson’s key skill vs wave-properties lab is…
choices: calculating and rearranging v = f × λ with units
only wiggling a rope with no numbers
pool.hint: Focus on the calculation and unit work.
pool.explain: Here you calculate and rearrange with coherent units. Rope and wave-type demos live in the properties lesson.

pool.prompt: λ = {a} m and f = {b} Hz. How much is v?
pool.hint: Multiply wavelength by frequency; the product is speed in m/s.

pool.prompt: Using λ = v × f instead of λ = v ÷ f…
pool.hint: Check which operation the rearrange needs.
pool.explain: Wavelength is speed divided by frequency. Multiplying inflates the answer.
